title: 12 Best Clay Alternatives in 2026 (Prices Checked)
summary: 12 Clay alternatives for 2026 compared on data, price, free tier and MCP/CLI support, with every price checked on the vendor's own page.
body_markdown:
## The 12 Clay alternatives, reviewed


### 1. Orange Slice


**Best for:** teams that want to describe a buying-signal list in plain English and pay per lookup instead of a fixed platform fee.


Orange Slice is an agentic enrichment spreadsheet ([YC S25](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/orange-slice) ). You describe the list in chat, and an agent builds the sheet, picks providers and runs it. Each column acts like an agent with one job. It pulls from 40+ data vendors plus web research, runs a cheapest-first waterfall for emails, and works in the web sheet, chat, API, CLI and MCP, including inside Claude Code ([homepage](https://orangeslice.ai/) ).


**Pricing (Oct 30, 2026):** Pay as you go is $0/month with a card, billed at vendor cost plus 25%. Pro is $99/month with $50 of usage included, vendor cost with no markup, and a 7-day trial. Agency is $499/month with $250 of usage and a workspace per client. A work email costs up to $0.11, with nothing charged on a miss ([pricing](https://www.orangeslice.ai/pricing) ).


**Where it falls short:** there's no free plan and no SOC 2 audit yet. Its provider catalog is smaller than Clay's. Read our honest head-to-head:[Orange Slice vs Clay](https://www.orangeslice.ai/compare/clay) .


### 2. Clay


**Best for:** teams that need the largest provider marketplace and are willing to learn a flexible table builder.


Clay has 150+ providers with waterfalls, Claygent AI agents, and unlimited seats on every plan. The Free plan includes 500 Actions and 100 Data Credits a month. Launch is $185/month billed monthly ($167 annually), and Growth is $495/month ($446 annually) ([clay.com/pricing](https://www.clay.com/pricing) , Oct 30, 2026). Clay states SOC 2 Type II. The trade-off is two meters (Actions and Data Credits) and a learning curve. Early-stage startups should check Clay's[Wedge program](https://www.clay.com/clay-for-startups) . For seed-stage options, see our[Clay alternative for YC startups](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/clay-alternative-for-yc-startups) .


### 3. Databar


**Best for:** teams that want a Clay-style table with lots of providers plus MCP and CLI access.


Databar lists 100+ providers, waterfalls and an AI web researcher. Build is $99/month for 5,000 credits and includes MCP, CLI, CRM integrations and bring-your-own API keys. Scale is $495/month for 50,000 credits. New workspaces get 100 trial credits, and failed requests aren't charged ([databar.ai/pricing](https://databar.ai/pricing) ).


### 4. Freckle


**Best for:** teams that want to start free with an AI enrichment table.


Freckle offers 40+ providers, waterfalls, web search and scraping. The Free plan has 250 credits and unlimited seats and tables. Build starts at $99/month with unlimited rows, an HTTP API and BYO keys ([freckle.io/pricing](https://www.freckle.io/pricing) ). It positions itself directly against Clay's action credits.


### 5. Apollo


**Best for:** teams that want a contact database, sequences and a dialer in one tool.


Apollo has its own large database, plus sequences, a built-in dialer and an MCP server on every plan ([apollo.io/product/mcp](https://www.apollo.io/product/mcp) ). It has a free plan, then per-user paid plans starting with Basic at $49/user/month billed annually. Credits are pooled and reset each cycle without rolling over (see our[Orange Slice vs Apollo](https://www.orangeslice.ai/compare/apollo) page, Apollo sources read Oct 24, 2026). It's a database first, not a flexible enrichment table. For signal-based outbound, see[Clay vs Apollo vs Orange Slice](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/clay-vs-apollo-vs-orange-slice) .


### 6. Unify


**Best for:** small teams that want AI outbound (data plus sequencing) and a free plan to start.


Unify's Free plan supports up to 3 seats with limited credits, a built-in database, sequencing and a dialer. Base is $20/seat/month with 800 credits, Pro is $60/seat/month with 2,400 credits and a 14-day trial, and website intent signals sit on the custom Business plan. It states SOC 2 Type II ([unifygtm.com/pricing](https://www.unifygtm.com/pricing) ).


### 7. Origami


**Best for:** hiring-signal prospecting with sending built in.


Origami aggregates postings from 100+ job boards, with keyword matching in descriptions and posting-age filters ([hiring signals](https://origami.chat/products/hiring-signals) ). It includes a sequencer and charges contact data at cost. Starter is $99/month with $165 of usage included, and a 7-day trial needs a card ([origami.chat/pricing](https://origami.chat/pricing) ).


### 8. Lusha


**Best for:** reps who want quick contact lookups from a browser extension.


Lusha's Free plan gives 40 credits a month. Starter is $49.90/month billed monthly ($37.45 annually) for 400 credits. An email costs 1 credit and a phone number 5, and one balance covers the app, extension, API and MCP ([lusha.com/pricing](https://www.lusha.com/pricing/) ). It's a lookup tool, not a workflow builder.


### 9. PhantomBuster


**Best for:** automating scraping and actions on LinkedIn and other web platforms.


PhantomBuster runs pre-built automations ("Phantoms"). According to its[support article](https://support.phantombuster.com/hc/en-us/articles/4494623647250) (prices "as of May 2026"), Start is $69/month ($56 annually), Grow $159 and Scale $439. There's a 14-day trial, then a limited free plan. It suits scraping and automation more than multi-provider enrichment.


### 10. HubSpot Breeze Intelligence (formerly Clearbit)


**Best for:** teams already on HubSpot that want enrichment inside the CRM.


HubSpot acquired Clearbit in 2023, and its enrichment now lives in HubSpot as Breeze Intelligence. According to HubSpot's[product catalog](https://legal.hubspot.com/hubspot-product-and-services-catalog) , contact and company enrichment no longer use HubSpot Credits on Starter, Professional and Enterprise editions. It's a natural choice if HubSpot is your system of record, but it isn't a standalone prospecting table.


### 11. TheirStack


**Best for:** raw job-posting and technographic data, including history.


TheirStack sells job and tech-stack data via an app, API, webhooks, MCP and datasets. It reports about 225M job records with ~305k new per day (vendor-reported). The API starts at $49/month, and app credits start at $109 one-time ([theirstack.com/en/pricing](https://theirstack.com/en/pricing) ). Pair it with our[job-postings prospecting guide](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/find-high-intent-b2b-prospects-job-postings) .


### 12. PredictLeads


**Best for:** developers who want company signals (jobs, news, tech) by API, webhooks or MCP.


PredictLeads reports job openings from 3M+ companies and millions of news events (vendor-reported). The first 100 credits are free, then it's pay per credit with a $40 monthly minimum ([predictleads.com/pricing](https://predictleads.com/pricing) ). It also integrates with Clay, so you can keep Clay and add PredictLeads signals.


## How to choose


1. **Name the job you hired Clay for.** Enrichment table, contact database, signals or sending? A replacement built for a different job won't fit, however good it is.
2. **Price a real run, not the plan.** Take 500 rows you'd actually enrich and estimate the cost on each vendor's page. Note what each charges on a miss.
3. **Check where it runs.** If your team works in Claude Code or other agents, MCP and CLI support matters (see the table).
4. **Check compliance early.** If buyers ask for SOC 2, filter on that first.
5. **Run a one-week pilot** on the same 100 accounts in two tools, and compare match rates and how long it takes to get a usable list.


If you're new to the category, start with[what an agentic enrichment spreadsheet is](https://www.orangeslice.ai/blog/what-is-an-agentic-enrichment-spreadsheet) .


## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to Clay in 2026?


There's no single winner; it depends on the job. Databar and Freckle are the closest Clay-style tables. Apollo and Unify bundle a database with sequencing. TheirStack and PredictLeads are best for raw signal data. Orange Slice suits teams that want to describe a signal-based list in plain English and pay per lookup.


### Is there a free Clay alternative?


Several tools have free plans or trial credits. As of Oct 30, 2026, Freckle offers 250 free credits, Unify has a free plan for up to three seats, Lusha gives 40 credits a month, Apollo has a free plan, and PredictLeads gives the first 100 credits free. Clay also has its own free plan.


### Which Clay alternatives support MCP?


Based on the vendors' own pages as of late October 2026, Orange Slice, Databar, Apollo, Lusha, TheirStack and PredictLeads list MCP support, and Clay lists a CLI, API and MCP (as read Oct 24, 2026). Other tools may add it, so check the vendor's docs if your team works in Claude Code or other AI agents.


### What happened to Clearbit?


HubSpot acquired Clearbit in 2023, and its enrichment is now part of HubSpot as Breeze Intelligence. According to HubSpot's product catalog, contact and company enrichment no longer use HubSpot Credits on Starter, Professional and Enterprise editions. Teams outside HubSpot usually look at the other tools in this list instead.


### Is Orange Slice cheaper than Clay?


It depends on volume. Orange Slice's Pay as you go plan has no monthly fee but charges vendor cost plus 25% per lookup, while Clay's Launch plan starts at $167 a month with credits included. Small or irregular volume may cost less without a fixed fee. Price a real 500-row run on both.
